picks.style: sanskrit recitation, tanpura drone, deep male voice, slow, incantatory, sparse
picks.why: The four-yuga refrain — country, village, family, the man himself — a built-in litany with descending force.

picks.style: martial dharma chant, dhol and shankha, strong male chorus, driving, exalted
picks.why: Blood running from the forehead into the mouth counted as a drinking of Soma; a warrior's hymn in four lines.

picks.style: devotional chant, tanpura and bansuri, warm male voice, reverent, unhurried
picks.why: The five bathings — ash, water, mantra, cow-dust, sun-shot rain — ending in the rain-bath equal to the Ganga.

picks.style: latin martyr hymn, low male schola with a single soprano, hand bell, austere, mounting, slow
picks.why: Eulalia counting her wounds as letters Christ writes on her: the purple of the blood speaks the sacred name.

picks.style: processional hymn, portative organ and boys' choir, bright, lilting, ceremonial
picks.why: Violets and blood-red crocuses gathered in mild winter to heap the baskets — an offering song with a clear refrain.

picks.style: ambrosian chant, unaccompanied male voices, resonant stone acoustic, grave, luminous, slow
picks.why: God beyond measure, light pouring out light; hymnic theology with a natural chant cadence.

picks.style: roman comic patter, tibia and clappers, wry male voice, brisk, confiding
picks.why: The lover who refuses to complain to the moon and addresses the audience instead — sharp, complete, funny.

picks.style: comic lover's aria, tibia and lyre, urgent male voice, sweeping, half-serious, accelerating
picks.why: Neither river nor mountain nor sea will stop him — a genuine vow-aria hiding inside a farce.

picks.style: old servant's song, plucked lyre and low drum, cracked weary female voice, slow, rueful
picks.why: Syra's burden: fourscore years and four, plus servitude, sweat and thirst.

picks.style: english pastoral ballad, acoustic guitar and fiddle, warm tenor, unhurried, tender
picks.why: You'll in your girls again be courted, and I go wooing in my boys — a whole marriage in a stanza.

picks.style: georgian air, harpsichord and viol, clear soprano, gentle, melancholy, measured
picks.why: The narcissus blooming at noon on the river bank and blasted by evening — a complete emblem.

picks.style: gothic ballad, bowed strings and low drone, hushed baritone, eerie, dragging tempo
picks.why: Three weird sisters horsed on staves, the grot where light never entered — vivid and self-contained.

picks.style: pastoral folk ballad, acoustic guitar, warm baritone, unhurried, contented
picks.why: The little field, the strayed lamb brought home under the arm, sleep under the beating rain.

picks.style: english elegy, solo piano and cello, restrained tenor, slow, aching
picks.why: Wound not thy cheeks, nor hurt that flowing hair — a deathbed address that needs no context.

picks.style: classical elegy, lute and viol, low male voice, grave, spare, measured
picks.why: O spare, Persephone, this guiltless head — Love, too much Love, is all thy suppliant's fault.

picks.style: satirical street chant, hand drum and aulos, jeering male chorus, repetitive, quickening
picks.why: The Metiochus jingle — he leads the army, bakes the bread, does all things, and will suffer for it at last.

picks.style: ancient memorial ode, lyre and low male chorus, solemn, stately, slow
picks.why: The epitaph for the fallen: God errs not, fails not; but man lies helpless in the hands of fate.

picks.style: riddle song, plucked lyre, single clear male voice, light, teasing, brisk
picks.why: Hesiod's extempore riddle of the racing hooves and the chariots breaking at the tomb of Zeus.
